title: Lecture 6. Fundamental Design Patterns II: Behavioral Patterns
summary: This lecture examines behavioral design patterns that manage object interactions and responsibilities in complex software systems. Students will explore the Observer, Visitor, Strategy, Command, and Template Method patterns, understanding their motivations, implementations, and trade-offs. The lecture emphasizes practical application of these patterns in object-oriented software construction and their role in creating flexible, maintainable architectures.
learningObjectives: Understand the purpose and characteristics of behavioral design patterns in managing object interactions
Apply the Observer pattern to implement event handling and notification systems
Utilize the Visitor pattern to add operations to object structures without modifying them
Implement the Strategy pattern to encapsulate and interchange algorithms
Apply the Command pattern to encapsulate actions and support undo/redo functionality
Recognize the Template Method pattern for defining algorithm skeletons
Evaluate trade-offs between different behavioral patterns and select appropriate patterns for specific design problems
Combine multiple patterns effectively in complex software systems

Understand how behavioral patterns manage object communication and responsibility distribution

subsections.title: What Are Behavioral Patterns?
keyPoints: Behavioral patterns focus on algorithms and responsibility assignment between objects
They characterize complex control flow that's difficult to follow at runtime
Shift focus from flow of control to object interconnections
Complement structural patterns by defining how objects collaborate
examples: Comparison with structural patterns (Adapter, Decorator) and creational patterns (Factory, Singleton)
Real-world analogy: organizational communication patterns in companies

sections.title: Observer Pattern: Event Handling and Notifications
learningGoals: Implement the Observer pattern to establish one-to-many dependencies
Apply Observer pattern for event-driven architectures
Understand the publish-subscribe mechanism

subsections.title: Observer Pattern Fundamentals
keyPoints: Intent: define one-to-many dependency so when one object changes state, dependents are notified automatically
Key participants: Subject (Observable) and Observer
Subject maintains list of observers and provides attach/detach methods
Observers implement update interface to receive notifications
Promotes loose coupling between subject and observers
examples: GUI event handling: button clicks notifying multiple listeners
Model-View-Controller (MVC): model notifying views of data changes
Stock market ticker: price changes notifying multiple displays
subsections.suggestedDiagram: UML class diagram showing Subject-Observer relationship with concrete implementations; sequence diagram showing notification flow

subsections.title: Observer Pattern Implementation
keyPoints: Subject interface: attach(Observer), detach(Observer), notify()
Observer interface: update() or update(Subject)
Push model: subject sends detailed data to observers
Pull model: subject notifies, observers query for data
Managing observer registration and lifecycle
examples: Code example in Eiffel or Java showing weather station notifying displays
Implementation of both push and pull notification models
Thread-safety considerations in concurrent environments
subsections.suggestedDiagram: Code structure diagram showing interface definitions and concrete implementations with notification flow arrows

subsections.title: Observer Pattern Trade-offs
keyPoints: Benefits: loose coupling, dynamic relationships, broadcast communication
Drawbacks: unexpected updates, potential performance issues with many observers
Memory leaks from forgotten observer registrations
Update cascades and ordering dependencies
Modern variations: event buses, reactive programming
examples: Memory leak scenario with GUI components
Performance analysis with 1 vs 1000 observers
Comparison with modern reactive frameworks (RxJava, ReactiveX)
subsections.suggestedDiagram: Comparison table showing benefits vs drawbacks; diagram showing potential cascade problem

exercises: Design an Observer-based notification system for a social media application
Identify and fix observer-related memory leaks in provided code
Compare push vs pull models for a specific use case

sections.title: Strategy Pattern: Algorithm Encapsulation
learningGoals: Apply Strategy pattern to make algorithms interchangeable
Eliminate conditional statements by using polymorphism
Configure objects with different behavioral variants

subsections.title: Strategy Pattern Fundamentals
keyPoints: Intent: define family of algorithms, encapsulate each one, make them interchangeable
Strategy varies independently from clients that use it
Key participants: Strategy interface, ConcreteStrategy classes, Context
Context maintains reference to Strategy and delegates algorithm execution
Replaces inheritance with composition for algorithm variation
examples: Sorting algorithms: QuickSort, MergeSort, BubbleSort as strategies
Payment processing: CreditCard, PayPal, Bitcoin payment strategies
Route calculation: fastest, shortest, scenic route strategies
subsections.suggestedDiagram: UML class diagram showing Context, Strategy interface, and multiple ConcreteStrategy implementations

subsections.title: Strategy Pattern Implementation and Use Cases
keyPoints: Strategy interface defines common algorithm interface
Context configured with ConcreteStrategy at runtime or construction
Eliminating switch/if-else statements through polymorphism
Strategy selection: client choice, factory, configuration
Combining with Factory pattern for strategy creation
examples: Text formatting: different strategies for HTML, Markdown, Plain text
Compression algorithms: ZIP, GZIP, BZIP2 strategies
Validation strategies: email, phone, credit card validators
subsections.suggestedDiagram: Code example showing before/after refactoring from conditionals to Strategy pattern; sequence diagram of strategy execution

subsections.title: Strategy vs State and Template Method
keyPoints: Strategy: clients choose algorithm; State: context changes behavior based on internal state
Strategy: composition-based; Template Method: inheritance-based
Strategy provides full algorithm replacement; Template Method allows step customization
When to use each pattern based on variability needs
Performance considerations: object creation vs inheritance overhead
examples: Side-by-side comparison of Strategy and Template Method for same problem
State pattern example showing automatic strategy switching
Decision matrix for pattern selection
subsections.suggestedDiagram: Comparison table highlighting key differences; parallel UML diagrams showing structural differences

exercises: Refactor a class with multiple conditional branches into Strategy pattern
Design a plugin system using Strategy pattern
Implement a game AI with different difficulty strategies

sections.title: Command Pattern: Action Encapsulation
learningGoals: Encapsulate requests as objects to enable parameterization and queuing
Implement undo/redo functionality using Command pattern
Apply Command pattern for transaction management and logging

subsections.title: Command Pattern Fundamentals
keyPoints: Intent: encapsulate request as object, allowing parameterization and queuing
Key participants: Command, ConcreteCommand, Invoker, Receiver
Command interface defines execute() method
ConcreteCommand binds Receiver with action
Invoker stores and executes commands without knowing details
Decouples sender from receiver of request
examples: GUI buttons and menu items executing commands
Text editor operations: cut, copy, paste, type
Remote control: each button is a command
Database transactions as commands
subsections.suggestedDiagram: UML class diagram showing Command pattern structure; sequence diagram showing command execution flow

subsections.title: Undo/Redo and Command History
keyPoints: Adding unexecute() or undo() method to Command interface
Maintaining command history stack for undo/redo
Memento pattern integration for state restoration
Handling non-reversible commands
Command composition for macro commands
Transaction boundaries and rollback
examples: Text editor with full undo/redo stack implementation
Graphics editor: move, resize, rotate commands with undo
Macro command combining multiple operations
Financial transaction system with rollback capability

keyPoints: Command queuing and scheduling
Logging and auditing through command serialization
Remote command execution (distributed systems)
Command pattern in CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation)
Combining with other patterns: Factory, Composite, Chain of Responsibility

Event sourcing: storing commands as event log
Network protocol: serializing commands for remote execution
Wizard/multi-step process using command chain

sections.title: Visitor Pattern: Operations on Object Structures
learningGoals: Apply Visitor pattern to add operations to object structures without modification
Implement double dispatch mechanism
Understand when Visitor pattern is appropriate vs alternatives

subsections.title: Visitor Pattern Fundamentals
keyPoints: Intent: represent operation to be performed on elements of object structure
Separates algorithm from object structure it operates on
Key participants: Visitor, ConcreteVisitor, Element, ConcreteElement, ObjectStructure
Double dispatch: operation depends on both visitor type and element type
Elements accept visitors and call back visitor's visit method
Adding new operations without modifying element classes
examples: Compiler AST: type checking, code generation, optimization as visitors
File system: size calculation, search, permission check as visitors
Shopping cart: pricing, tax calculation, shipping as visitors
Document structure: rendering, spell-check, word count as visitors
subsections.suggestedDiagram: UML class diagram showing Visitor pattern structure with double dispatch; collaboration diagram showing visitor traversal

subsections.title: Visitor Pattern Implementation
keyPoints: Visitor interface with visit methods for each concrete element type
Element interface with accept(Visitor) method
ConcreteElement implements accept by calling visitor.visit(this)
ObjectStructure provides iteration over elements
Traversal strategies: depth-first, breadth-first
Accumulating results during traversal
examples: Expression tree evaluation using visitor
HTML DOM manipulation with different visitors
Graph traversal with visitor pattern
Code example showing visitor implementation in Eiffel/Java
subsections.suggestedDiagram: Sequence diagram showing double dispatch mechanism; code structure showing visitor and element implementations

subsections.title: Visitor Pattern Trade-offs and Alternatives
keyPoints: Benefits: easy to add new operations, related operations grouped together
Drawbacks: difficult to add new element types (breaks all visitors)
Violates encapsulation: visitor needs access to element internals
When to use: stable element hierarchy, frequently changing operations
Alternatives: instanceof checks, method overloading, pattern matching
Modern language features: pattern matching, multimethods
examples: Comparison with adding methods directly to element classes
Impact analysis: adding new operation vs adding new element type
Visitor pattern in languages with pattern matching (Scala, Rust)
Acyclic Visitor pattern for more flexibility
subsections.suggestedDiagram: Decision tree for choosing Visitor vs alternatives; comparison table showing trade-offs

exercises: Implement visitors for an expression tree (evaluate, print, optimize)
Design a file system visitor for different operations
Analyze the impact of adding a new element type to an existing visitor hierarchy

sections.title: Template Method Pattern
learningGoals: Define algorithm skeleton in base class with customizable steps
Apply Template Method for code reuse through inheritance
Distinguish Template Method from Strategy pattern

subsections.title: Template Method Pattern Overview
keyPoints: Intent: define skeleton of algorithm, defer some steps to subclasses
Base class implements template method calling abstract/hook methods
Subclasses override specific steps without changing algorithm structure
Hollywood Principle: 'Don't call us, we'll call you'
Hook methods provide optional extension points
Primitive operations must be implemented by subclasses
examples: Framework lifecycle methods: initialize(), process(), cleanup()
Data processing pipeline: read(), parse(), validate(), store()
Game AI: collectInput(), update(), render()
HTTP request handling: authenticate(), authorize(), execute(), respond()
subsections.suggestedDiagram: UML class diagram showing abstract class with template method and primitive operations; flowchart showing algorithm steps

subsections.title: Template Method vs Strategy
keyPoints: Template Method: inheritance-based, compile-time binding
Strategy: composition-based, runtime flexibility
Template Method: partial algorithm customization; Strategy: full algorithm replacement
Template Method: simpler for closely related variants
Strategy: better for independent, interchangeable algorithms
Combining both patterns for maximum flexibility
examples: Same problem solved with both patterns
Migration path from Template Method to Strategy
Hybrid approach using both patterns together
subsections.suggestedDiagram: Side-by-side comparison of Template Method and Strategy implementations; decision flowchart for pattern selection

exercises: Implement a data import framework using Template Method
